newsitem.title: CANADA: Bema drops on new Chile drilling results.
newsitem.headline: Bema drops on new Chile drilling results.

text.p: Shares in Bema Gold Corp dropped in heavy trading Friday on new drilling results, analysts said.
Stock in the Vancouver-based company fell C$1.05 to C$7.85, or almost 12 percent, by midday before rebounding slightly to C$8.10.
Analysts said investors were disappointed with drilling results from the company's Cerro Casale project in Chile.
On Thursday, Bema said 14 new drill holes at the project showed an average of 1.24 grams of gold per tonne and 0.40 percent copper.
"The market wants to see some wide high grade intersections," said mining analyst Doug Leishman with Yorkton Securities.
But Bema has concentrated on defining the outside edges of the gold and copper deposit, not the richer centre, Leishman said.
Bema has 49 percent of the project and Arizona Star Resource Corp, which is controlled by Bema, has 51 percent.
